hops.afterHeading: What transduces force in the lung and the artery
hops.title: Count your pulse sitting, then standing
hops.text: Sit for a minute, rest two fingertips on the inside of your wrist, and count your pulse for fifteen seconds. Then stand up and count again. Heart rate typically rises by about 10 to 15 beats per minute on standing, so you may count a few extra beats. Standing lets gravity shift 500 to 800 millilitres of blood into your legs and abdomen. Wall stretch at the carotid sinus and aortic arch drops, the baroreceptors fire less, and the brainstem eases the vagal brake while turning up sympathetic drive. If standing up ever makes you feel faint, skip this one.

sources.citation: Campos Munoz A, Vohra S, Gupta M. Orthostasis. StatPearls, 2023 (PMID 30422533)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A college student standing by a sunlit desk, checking their wrist pulse with two fingertips.
image.caption: Standing shifts blood to the legs, arterial stretch falls, baroreceptors fire less, and the heart speeds up.

hops.afterHeading: A map of the organs in the brainstem, sharpened by inhibition
hops.title: Oto-tricho-tussia: when a stray hair in the ear canal sets off a cough
hops.text: A 51-year-old man had over six weeks of coughing spasms that resisted antibiotics, a steroid inhaler and reflux pills. Ear specialists found a single hair on his eardrum. Removing it stopped his throat tickle at once, he reported. A small branch of the vagus, Arnold's nerve, carries touch from the ear canal to the brainstem, where it can set off the cough reflex. In one study, swabbing the ear canal made 2 percent of healthy volunteers cough, against 25.5 percent of adults with chronic cough. The case authors proposed the name oto-tricho-tussia (ear, hair, cough).

sources.citation: Castro RA, Zalvan CH, Berzofsky C. Oto-tricho-tussia: hair in the ear canal as a cause of chronic cough. Case Reports in Otolaryngology, 2020 (PMC7150714)
Dicpinigaitis PV, Kantar A, Enilari O, Paravati F. Prevalence of Arnold nerve reflex in adults and children with chronic cough. Chest, 2018 (PMID 29197546)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A barbershop shelf with a brass comb, a single dark hair on a folded white towel, and a steaming mug of tea.
image.caption: A stray hair on the eardrum can stimulate the vagus nerve's ear branch and, in some people, set off coughing.

hops.afterHeading: From afferent to behaviour: stretch, satiety and what the trial evidence covers
hops.title: Why chicken soup fills you more than chicken with a glass of water
hops.text: In a 1999 study, 24 women ate a 1,128-kilojoule chicken-and-rice starter 17 minutes before lunch. A casserole with a 356-gram glass of water on the side did no better than the casserole alone. After a soup made from the same ingredients and water, the women ate 27 percent fewer calories at lunch than after casserole and water, with no catch-up eating at dinner. A 2012 Nottingham study used roast chicken and vegetables. On MRI, water drunk with the solid meal left the stomach quickly, while the blended soup kept stomach volume up longer; in a separate group, the soup lowered hunger.

sources.citation: Rolls BJ, Bell EA, Thorwart ML. Water incorporated into a food but not served with a food decreases energy intake in lean women. Am J Clin Nutr, 1999 (PMID 10500012)
Marciani L et al. Preventing gastric sieving by blending a solid/water meal enhances satiation in healthy humans. J Nutr, 2012 (PMID 22649258)

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: Two lunch trays side by side, one with chicken, rice and a glass of water, the other with a steaming bowl of chicken-and-rice soup.
image.caption: Blended into soup, the water stays with the food, so the stomach stays fuller for longer.
